en.headline: Tourism Board to review Peak light trail after residents raise concerns
en.dek: The board said it would conduct broader consultation to refine arrangements for the planned installations along Lugard and Harlech Roads, aiming for a better balance with environmental protection and local needs.
body: The Hong Kong Tourism Board said on Sunday it would continue close communication with residents and other stakeholders and carry out broader consultation to review the overall arrangements of a planned light-effect project on The Peak.

The board originally intended to install small, low-glare light devices at selected points along the walking trails on Lugard Road and Harlech Road, operating between 7pm and 10pm, as part of a new light show tied to the Hong Kong WinterFest and intended to replace A Symphony of Lights. It said the project had been discussed with district officials and residents on several occasions and was planned as a 12-month trial.

In a statement the board said it understood and valued residents' views. It pledged to refine the details so as to achieve a more appropriate balance between tourism development, protection of the natural environment and residents' needs, and would announce updated arrangements in due course.

zh.headline: 旅發局就山頂燈影項目進行更廣泛諮詢 檢視安排
zh.dek: 局方表示明白並重視居民意見，會繼續緊密溝通，檢視盧吉道及夏力道一帶燈影效果項目的整體安排，務求在旅遊發展、環境保護及居民需要之間取得更適切平衡。
body: 香港旅遊發展局周日表示，鑒於近日市民就山頂燈影項目表示關注，局方會繼續與居民及相關持份者保持緊密溝通，並進行更廣泛的諮詢，以檢視項目的整體安排及優化項目細節。
旅發局原定計劃於山頂盧吉道及夏力道一帶推出燈影效果項目，於步行徑部分指定位置設置小型低眩光燈光裝置，晚上七時至十時運作，並配合「香港繽紛冬日巡禮」的全新光影匯演一併推出，取代「幻彩詠香江」。局方指項目原訂試行十二個月，並曾多次向附近居民及區議員介紹內容。
局方強調明白並重視居民意見，將適時公布項目的最新安排，務求在推動旅遊發展、保護自然環境及兼顧居民需要之間取得更適切的平衡。
